clue.text: Nasty about Times section for food

indicators.note: about means the word for nasty goes round the letters for times

parts.note: nasty means vile
T is time, doubled for the plural as with pp for pages

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the food pages of The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a less common spelling of VICTUALS; the wordplay settles the order of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal spelling of victuals, meaning provisions or things to eat.

clue.text: Outspoken against old state

parts.note: V, versus, means against
Cal is an abbreviation of California, a US state

explanation.surface: A politician speaks out against the old state.
explanation.definitionFit: Being vocal means expressing opinions loudly and freely.

clue.text: Maybe Tom has to capture small image

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny folklore hero, so Tom hints at his surname
to nail someone is to catch them

explanation.surface: Perhaps a tomcat has to catch a small picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a cat or a name; it is Tom Thumb.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail is a miniature version of a picture or a computer preview.

clue.text: Stand at the front of church

definitions.text: Stand at the front of church

parts.words: Stand at the front of church
parts.note: a reading desk on a stand placed at the front of a church, where Bible passages are read

explanation.surface: A command to take a position before the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' reads as a verb telling someone where to go, but it is the noun for a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is the reading stand from which lessons are read in church.

clue.text: Dropped apple-core into mud

indicators.note: into puts the core letter inside the word for mud

parts.note: silt is fine mud deposited by water

indicators.note: the core is the middle letter of apple

explanation.surface: Someone dropped an apple core into the mud.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilt is the British past participle of spill, as in let fall.

clue.text: Town station in El Salvador

parts.note: ES is the international vehicle code for El Salvador

explanation.surface: A railway station somewhere in the Central American country of El Salvador.
explanation.walkthrough: STAINES is a town in Surrey, just west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Staines is an English town on the Thames near Heathrow, an example of a town.

clue.text: Get rid of group of terrorists we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for a group of terrorists is spoken, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: a cell is a small unit of a terrorist network

explanation.surface: We are told about a plan to eliminate a terrorist group.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell something is to dispose of it for money, so to get rid of it.

clue.text: "Silvers swallows arsenic" — a story

indicators.note: swallows means the two silvers take arsenic inside them

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, so two silvers are AG twice
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about the Silvers family being poisoned, presented as a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga saga is a British genre of novel about middle-class country life, named for the Aga range cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aga saga is a kind of popular novel, so it is a type of story.

clue.text: Report interference?

definitions.meaning: a report is a loud bang, a sudden sound
unwanted disturbance on a signal, as in static on a line

explanation.surface: Is a news story meddling?
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is both a loud sound and random disturbance in a signal.

clue.text: Astonishing cup result for Bobby Moore at Wembley?

indicators.note: astonishing is read as stunning the letters of cup result into a new order

explanation.surface: England's World Cup win at Wembley in 1966 under captain Bobby Moore was astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bobby Moore, England's 1966 World Cup-winning football captain, has a bronze statue outside Wembley Stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: The bronze figure of Moore outside the stadium is an example of a statue, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Ill-bred fellow's abrupt and unfriendly with old leader

indicators.note: abrupt is read as cut short, so the word for the ill-bred fellow loses its last letter

parts.note: a churl is a rude, ill-bred fellow; the 's stands for is
chill means cold and unfriendly

explanation.surface: A boorish man is curt and frosty towards a former leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abrupt' looks like a description of manner but it docks the end of CHURL to give CHUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Winston Churchill was the British wartime Prime Minister, a former national leader.

clue.text: What could be cast in gold for farewell

indicators.note: in places the thing that is cast inside the symbol for gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is thrown or cast, as in 'the die is cast'

explanation.surface: Something cast in gold, such as a medallion, given as a parting gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests metal-casting, but it is the throwing of a die.
explanation.definitionFit: A French word for goodbye used in English as a formal parting.

clue.text: Trio belt out operatic words

indicators.note: out signals the letters of trio belt are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Three singers belt out their lines in an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The libretto is the text that is set to music in an opera.

clue.text: Bring round nature award we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words for nature and award are spoken, giving something that sounds like the entry

parts.note: way can mean nature or manner, and a cup is an award; said together they sound like the entry

explanation.surface: A wildlife prize is presented, as some radio report tells us.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone round is to revive them from unconsciousness.

clue.text: Client standing up in leisure suit

indicators.note: standing up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A customer stands up wearing a casual leisure suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is a customer of a service, much as a client is.

clue.text: Spartan queen has one going for new calendar?

indicators.note: one letter going and another taken in its place, so the letter for one is swapped out

parts.note: spartan means austere or plain
I is the Roman numeral one
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: A queen of ancient Sparta has one replaced by a new calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spartan queen' reads as Helen or Leda, but Spartan is the adjective for austere.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall or desk planner is a type of calendar for scheduling, hence the question mark.

clue.text: One against redevelopment of top resort

indicators.note: redevelopment of means the letters of top resort are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A campaigner opposes rebuilding a leading holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A protestor is someone who objects to or demonstrates against something.

clue.text: Excellent gunners and engineers

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Praise for the artillery and engineer regiments.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare in an old-fashioned sense means unusually good or splendid.

clue.text: Old man in Sudan beaten up in prison

indicators.note: in puts the old man inside the rearranged letters
beaten up means the letters of Sudan are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, the old man

explanation.surface: An elderly man is assaulted in a Sudanese jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Spandau was the Berlin prison where Nazi war criminals such as Rudolf Hess were held.
explanation.definitionFit: Spandau is the name of a former jail in Berlin, an example of a prison.

clue.text: Oscar met Brad dancing with a beautiful person

indicators.note: dancing has the letters moving about into a new order

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: At the Oscars someone met Brad Pitt and danced with a stunning partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamboat is an informal term for a very attractive person.

clue.text: Dread regular contributors to rag week

indicators.note: the letters contributing at regular intervals, every second letter of rag week

explanation.surface: Students fear the people who always write for the student paper during charity week.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag week is a British university week of charity stunts and fundraising.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is reverential fear, so it can stand for dread as a noun.

clue.text: One promising love and money amongst older men

parts.note: O, nil in tennis scoring, is love

indicators.note: amongst places the letter for money within the word for older

parts.note: big as in big sister or brother means older
L, for libra, is the pound sign
OR, other ranks, are the ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Someone promises affection and cash to older gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'older men' reads as one phrase, but it splits in two: 'big' as in big brother, then 'men' as the other ranks of the army.
explanation.definitionFit: An obligor is a party who binds themselves by a legal promise or bond to another.

clue.text: Work with artist hiding evil thug

parts.note: to go is to work or function

indicators.note: hiding means the word for artist keeps the word for evil within it

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist
ill means evil, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: A painter conceals a wicked brute in his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorilla is slang for a big, brutish heavy, a thug.

clue.text: Full traveller meeting obstruction before beginning to eat

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller
a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'

indicators.note: beginning to picks just the first letter of eat

explanation.surface: A sales rep blocked from starting a meal is already stuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: A commercial traveller is a travelling salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means filled to capacity, especially well fed.

clue.text: Group of soldiers also included in scheme

indicators.note: included in places the word for also within the word for scheme

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
too means also

explanation.surface: A unit of troops is also part of the battle plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small army unit, a subdivision of a company.

clue.text: Old forward is good player?

parts.note: ex means former or old
pert means saucy or forward

explanation.surface: A former striker in football is a fine player, or so we ask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' suggests a football position but means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is a skilled performer, and a good player is one example, hence the query.

clue.text: Penny's excited over picture

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny; the 's stands for is
hot can mean excited or aroused
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A girl called Penny is thrilled about an image.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo is a photograph, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Preserved forged medal (British Empire Medal)

indicators.note: forged means made up or falsified, so the letters are hammered into a new shape

parts.note: BEM is the abbreviation for British Empire Medal

explanation.surface: A fake decoration, the British Empire Medal in particular, has been kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A body that is embalmed has been treated with chemicals so that it does not decay.

clue.text: Rector leaves choice food for wine

indicators.note: leaves means the letter for rector departs from the word for choice food

parts.note: a morsel is a tasty bite of food

explanation.surface: A clergyman leaves behind a fine meal in favour of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosel is a German white wine named after the river valley where it is made.

clue.text: Storage units Kelvin installed in Norfolk town

indicators.note: installed in puts the letter for Kelvin inside the town name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, an English county
K is the symbol for kelvin

explanation.surface: Data-storage equipment from a firm named Kelvin is put in an East Anglian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Disks are computer devices that hold data.

clue.text: Leave out note in books

indicators.note: in places the note within the books

parts.note: OT, Old Testament, is a set of books
mi is a note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Skip the note in the books.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to exclude or fail to include.

clue.text: Deliberately offend leader leaving walk

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which departs from the word for walk

parts.note: a stroll is a leisurely walk

explanation.surface: A man deliberately insults the head of state as he leaves on a walkabout.
explanation.definitionFit: Online, trolling is posting provocative messages meant to upset or anger people.

clue.text: Secretive men eating fox and woolly creatures

indicators.note: eating means the secretive men take the fox inside

parts.note: Freemasons, masons, are known for their secret rites
tod is a Scots and dialect word for fox

explanation.surface: A secret society dines on fox and sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastodons were extinct elephant-like mammals, some shaggy-coated, so woolly beasts.

clue.text: Warning words after Republican's scrap before court

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
an iota is a tiny scrap or jot

explanation.surface: A Republican politician has a scrap and then faces a court, after warnings.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading the Riot Act is a British idiom for a stern telling-off, after the 1714 law read aloud to disperse crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: To read someone the riot act is to give them a severe reprimand or caution.

clue.text: Lunatics in a tizzy without a medicinal preparation

indicators.note: in a tizzy means flustered, so the letters of lunatics are thrown into confusion
without says the letter a is dropped from the mix

explanation.surface: Madmen in a panic go without their medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Linctus is a syrupy cough medicine.
